$comment: EXTRUDED signs only. A flat sign — which is nearly all of them — is not here and needs no build step at all: it is a `sign({ type: 'flat', ... })` call in the builder, rendered in the browser (src/render/sign-plates.ts). This file is the recipe for the few whose letters genuinely stand off the wall, built by tools/signs.ts (which the bake calls) with Blender. The GLBs live under public/models/signs and are gitignored: assets are generated, the recipe is what is kept. A builder names the file in `sign({ type: 'extruded', model: 'signs/x.glb' })`, or a landmark entry in its `file` field as `models/signs/x.glb`.

san-francisco.note: Ghirardelli Square's roof sign, read from the bay: mixed case, bulbs along the letters, standing on the steel lattice drawn by the `ghirardelliSign` builder. Extruded because the bulbs ARE the sign — a flat one could not carry them. 2026-10-17: lit 'front' — with 'self' the letter faces emitted by day and the word blew out to a white bar; the bulbs carry the night.
Ripley's at 175 Jefferson: the yellow sign over the arched entrance. Bold italic, mixed case, painted rather than steel — so a yellow, unmetallic material rather than the default polished one.
